speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying your specific medical history; you mentioned a significant past, so what chronic conditions or previous surgeries have you endured? Additionally, how long has this gait and limb ataxia been affecting you?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see; this clumsiness suggests a coordination issue. When you walk, do you tend to veer significantly to the right, or does your body swivel like a top? Also, have you noticed any double vision or slurred speech lately?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast; REQUEST TEST: CSF analysis for oligoclonal bands. Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, I suspect you may have developed progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can present with ataxia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
